question: The chemical reaction Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s) represents which type of reaction?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction **Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)** is an example of a **displacement reaction**.
 
• In a displacement reaction, a more **reactive element** displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• Here, **iron (Fe)** is more reactive than **copper (Cu)**, so iron displaces copper from copper sulfate (CuSO4).
 
• This results in the formation of **iron sulfate (FeSO4)** and **copper (Cu)**.
 
• Displacement reactions are also known as **single replacement reactions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Combustion reaction**__

 __
 
• A **combustion reaction** involves the burning of a substance in the presence of oxygen to produce heat and light.
 
• Common examples include the burning of fuels like **methane (CH4)** in oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water.
 
 
 
• **Combination reaction**__
 __
 
• In a **combination reaction**, two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• An example is the reaction between **hydrogen (H2)** and **oxygen (O2)** to form water (H2O).
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement reaction**__
 
 
• A **double displacement reaction** involves the exchange of ions between two compounds to form new compounds.
 
• An example is the reaction between **sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **silver nitrate (AgNO3)** to form **sodium nitrate (NaNO3)** and **silver chloride (AgCl)**.
